sections.heading: C - Safe Driving Tips
sections.markdown:
## C - Safe Driving Tips

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Safe driving opens with a fixed visual search in every direction, since spotting trouble early buys time to adjust speed or position, so keep your eyes roaming and never stare [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Aim your gaze down your path to read the road, its users, and its conditions in time for calm decisions, ideally scanning 20 to 30 seconds ahead and refusing to tuck behind tall vehicles that steal your view [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Sweep the sides for crossers and the mirrors for trailers, with rear checks mandatory before lane changes, slowdowns, stops, and intersection entries [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Manage speed for roads and traffic, keep a real following gap, obey posted limits, and glance at the speedometer about once a minute [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Unposted Kentucky limits run 65 MPH on interstates and parkways, 55 MPH on other state highways, 35 MPH in business and residential districts, 15 MPH in public-use off-street lots, with the transportation secretary able to raise select highways to 70 MPH [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
Never outdrive your headlights at night, and when heavy rain, snow, or fog cuts sight to 100 feet, cap speed at 25 miles per hour on low beams [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
Creep past intersection greenery, parked cars, signs, and buildings that hide side traffic, and enter hills and curves slow enough to halt for a stalled or crawling vehicle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Slow before every curve to a pace that carries slight steady throttle throughout, slowing further for weak grip, followers, and blind exits, since hard mid-curve braking breaks traction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
Ease off at the first rain, snow, sleet, or ice, because slick rubber stops longer, turns wider, and skids or floats at speed or downhill, so postpone sharp braking and turning until grip returns, pumping gently without anti-lock brakes and pressing steadily with them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
Hydroplaning floats steering tires onto pooled water like skis with zero road contact, so slow down on wet roads, keep tires firm and treaded, and never drive through large standing water but reroute instead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
Total stopping distance spans realization to rest under ideal conditions, grows with speed, and starts with perception time averaging 3/4 second to 1 second in alert drivers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A03
Reaction time from gas to brake averages 3/4 second to 1 second, and braking distance from pedal to rest runs about 158 feet from 50 mph on dry pavement with sound brakes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A03
A space cushion in every direction buys reaction time, so guard open room around your car at all times [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A03
Rear-enders top the crash list because tailgating blinds and starves reaction, so keep at least 4 seconds to the leader, since unreasonably tight following breaks the law [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A03
Time your gap by counting one-thousand-one through one-thousand-four from the leader's passing of a fixed point, slowing and recounting until you trail by no less than four seconds [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A03
Stretch the gap on slick roads, behind big rigs, buses, campers, and trailers, at night and in foul weather, behind railroad-stopping buses and hazmat haulers, and behind quick-jinking motorcycles [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A04
When a follower wants past, ease off the gas and slow as needed so the passer gains room to slip in ahead of you [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A05
Hold side room for lateral escapes where others can see you, shun lingering in blind spots by speeding up or dropping back, and give oncoming traffic its full half [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A05
Open space for freeway mergers by shifting or slowing, pad pedestrians, children, and cyclists, slide outside for tractor-trailers, gap parked cars against doors and pull-outs, and on interstates swing left early past shoulder parkers before returning right [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A05
Steady speed, early signals, and extra nose room before slowing or turning help tailgaters hold off and buy you reaction time [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A05
Cover others' mistakes by speeding, slowing, swerving, or stopping as the moment demands so the crash never happens [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A05
Back with extra care for the blind rear, shunning reverse entries into traffic and borrowing a ground guide when you can [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A05
Past your interstate exit, never back up or spin around; roll on to the next exit and circle back [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A05
Communication means broadcasting your place and plans while keeping your car conspicuous to all [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A06
Light headlamps from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, plus rainy, snowy, foggy, and dusky spells, sun-glare runs, and any moment others look dim, since dim-to-you means dim-to-them [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A06
Tap the horn lightly for lane-drifting walkers and cyclists, cutters-off mid-pass, and drifting or blind drivers, reserving the horn for real messages since blasts startle and anger, and never honk near blind pedestrians [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A06
Signal before every direction change and slowdown, covering lane moves, passes, turns, merges, turnabouts, freeway entries and exits, curb departures, and roadside stops [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A06
Signal every single time even when the road looks empty, because the unseen car kills, checking blind spots over your shoulder, remembering signals grant no right-of-way, cancelling promptly, and using mechanical signals only since hand signals are banned [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A06
Brake lights voice your slowdown, so signal before slowing for turn-offs lacking their own lanes and for parking or turning ahead of intersections [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0062]
